intro.title: MineSweeper Project Overview
intro.desc: MineSweeper is built with C++ and EasyX. The project uses a Scene + SceneManager architecture to manage menu, difficulty/custom setup, and gameplay states. Core gameplay includes random mine generation, board-state management, recursive safe-area reveal, match timer, and quick restart flow.

text: Core Gameplay Implementation: The core module is MineBoard, which tracks mine distribution, visible player state, and neighbor hint numbers.
Empty-cell clicks trigger recursive chain reveal, mine clicks end the game, and clearing all non-mine cells results in victory.
Rendering and Interaction: The project is built on EasyX (graphics.h) and message/event handling with ExMessage.
State Separation: Main menu, difficulty/custom setup, and gameplay are separated into scene subclasses and orchestrated by SceneManager.
Board Logic: MineBoard handles mine placement, number calculation, reveal/flag actions, win/loss checks, and final board display.
Main Features and Interaction Flow:
Main Menu: Start enters gameplay; Setting opens difficulty/custom configuration.
Difficulty and Custom Mode: Presets include Easy/Normal/Hard/Expert. Custom mode supports Row/Col/Mine input through keyboard editing.
First-Click Safety: Mines are generated on the first left click (not at launch), and the timer starts at that moment to avoid instant-death openings.
Reveal and Expansion: Clicking empty cells triggers recursive neighborhood expansion (flood-fill style).
Flagging and Counter: Right click toggles flags and updates remaining mine/flag counter display.
Win/Loss Display: On failure or win, the board reveals full mine and mark status for result feedback.
Restart/Exit: Restart reinitializes board data; Exit returns to menu.
Implementation Highlights:

Scene + SceneManager Lifecycle Control

Scene defines behavior contracts. SceneManager keeps current scene pointer and switches with a strict order: on_exit -> switch -> on_enter.
Input/update/render dispatch is centralized to keep logic clear and extensible.

Event Handling + UI Button

Button maintains a clickable RECT region with Idle/Hovered/Pushed states.
Click confirmation is performed on mouse-up after press, reducing accidental triggers. A hold-state mechanism is used for difficulty-selection highlighting.

Delayed Mine Generation Strategy

Mine placement is delayed until first left click via set_mine(y, x), then timer starts.
When free area is sufficient, a protected 3x3 safe zone can be reserved around the first click to improve opening experience.

Board Data Model: Three 2D Grids

MineBoard uses separate grids for mine map, visible state, and neighbor count.
Board storage includes a padded boundary to simplify neighborhood traversal and reduce boundary-condition branching.

Reveal Algorithm: Recursive Flood Fill

Safe unopened cells are revealed and expanded recursively when neighbor count is zero.
Potential Improvements:

Resource and Logic Decoupling

Earlier implementation loaded many global IMAGE resources in one place, which raises maintenance cost.
A centralized ResourceManager can better control loading, cache, and lifecycle.

Custom Input State Edge Cases

Certain custom-setting button hold/reset timing paths are easy to break and can be further simplified with stronger state encapsulation.

General Refactoring

Prefer std::unique_ptr<Scene> for scene ownership and move large implementation blocks from headers into .cpp files.
